Professional services / Law firms & legal practices

Conflict checks, hearing dates and drafting, run from one system

Law firms need control more than reach. Advocates in India cannot solicit work or advertise under the Bar Council of India Rules, so we focus on what happens after a client approaches you: recorded conflict checks, engagement terms, a hearing diary, template-based drafting and an assistant that answers only from your own precedents.

The challenge

What makes law firms & legal practices different.

01

Conflict checks rely on emailing every partner or searching a spreadsheet by client name, missing group companies and opposing parties.

02

Next hearing dates live in diaries and clerks' registers, and clients call the office to find out what happened in court.

03

Routine drafts start from the last similar file, which can carry another client's names, facts or outdated clauses.

04

Years of opinions and pleadings are hard to find, and public AI tools cannot be trusted with privileged material.

05

Time on appearances and advisory work is recorded late, so fees are delayed, disputed or written off.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for law firms & legal practices.

01

Recorded conflict checks

Client, related entity and opposing party searches across past matters, with every possible match reviewed and the decision recorded by the conflicts partner before a matter number is issued.

02

Engagement letters from approved clauses

Scope, fee basis, GST, confidentiality and termination terms assembled from the firm's own wording, edited and approved by the partner, then sent for e-signature.

03

Hearing diary and next-date reminders

One entry after each hearing drives preparation tasks for the team, a morning court-wise list for advocates and clerks, and a short date-only update for clients who opted in.

04

Document assembly from firm templates

Legal notices, agreements, affidavits and routine applications generated from approved templates with matter data, highlighting every missing field and deviation for the drafting lawyer.

05

Precedent assistant with ethical walls

Answers drawn only from the firm's own precedents and opinions, each with a citation to the source paragraph, and access that mirrors matter staffing and any information barriers.

06

Timesheets and fee follow-up

Daily time nudges, partner-approved invoices with GST details, including the reverse-charge note where it applies, and courteous reminders that pause automatically for disputed or sensitive clients.

Conflict, independence and KYC checksAdvanced5–8 weeks

Client acceptance: conflicts, independence and KYC

New clients and matters are checked against the firm's own records for conflicts, auditor independence and, where the law requires it, client due diligence, with every possible match and decision recorded before work starts.

Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Conflict checks in many firms are an email to all partners or a spreadsheet search by client name. Related companies, directors and opposing parties are missed, independence for audit clients is checked inconsistently, and there is no record of who cleared what, when and why.

Trigger

An intake partner submits a new client or matter form listing the client, group companies, directors or promoters, opposing or counter parties and the nature of the work.

How it runs

  • Normalize names, covering spelling variants, initials and forms such as Pvt Ltd and Private Limited, and expand the search with group companies and directors given on the form.
  • Search current and past clients, matters, adverse parties and audit clients in the firm's records, returning exact and fuzzy matches with the reason each one surfaced.
  • For CA firms, flag audit clients where the proposed service raises an independence question, and flag work within PMLA-specified activities for KYC.
  • Where KYC applies, send a secure upload request for identity, address and beneficial ownership documents and record verification status; nothing sensitive is requested over chat.
  • Show results on a review screen where the conflicts or engagement partner records clear, clear with conditions or decline, with reasons.
  • Issue the matter or engagement number only after clearance, and pass the record to the engagement letter step.

Human checkpoint

A designated conflicts partner in a law firm, or the engagement partner in a CA firm, reviews every possible match and decides. Any suspicion-related judgment under PMLA stays with the principal officer. The system never auto-clears a check, and nothing about a suspicion is shared with the client.

Tools

SSupabasePPythonRRetoolnn8nSSlack

Systems it connects

  • Matter or engagement register
  • Practice management system
  • Document management system
  • Client master in Tally or the firm's ERP

Data & consent

Conflict data is limited to names, relationships and short matter descriptions. KYC documents sit in an access-controlled store, retained for the period PMLA requires, generally five years after the relationship ends. Search logs show who searched and when, and results are visible only to the risk team and responsible partner.

What we deliver

  • Conflict search service over the firm's client and matter records
  • Review and decision screen with an audit trail
  • KYC request and status tracker for PMLA-specified engagements
  • Acceptance rules configured with the risk partner

How we measure it

  • Working days from intake to acceptance decision
  • New matters with a recorded conflict decision
  • Possible matches reviewed per check
  • KYC files complete before work starts

Proposal and engagement termsStandard4–6 weeks

Proposals and engagement letters from approved libraries

Proposals, statements of work and engagement letters start from the firm's approved templates and rate card. AI drafts narrative sections only where the firm allows it, and a partner edits and approves every document before it goes for signature.

Marketing & creative agencies · Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Partners rebuild proposals and engagement letters from the last similar file, which carries old client names, outdated scope wording and inconsistent fee terms. Agencies and consultancies lose days on largely reusable proposals; law and CA firms skip written terms on smaller matters and later disagree about scope.

Trigger

A qualified opportunity or a cleared matter is marked ready for terms in the CRM or matter register, with scoping notes attached.

How it runs

  • Select the template for the engagement type, such as retainer, project, litigation matter, statutory audit, tax filing or advisory, and fill client, team, timeline and fee fields from the record.
  • Retrieve approved content from the firm's own library, such as methodology sections, team profiles and past scope language, filtered by service line and permission.
  • For agencies and consultancies, have an LLM draft context, approach and plan sections from the scoping notes and retrieved content, marking every generated passage.
  • For law and CA firms, assemble wording only from approved clauses: scope, exclusions, fees, GST, confidentiality and, for audits, the terms auditing standards require in writing.
  • Check for leftover names from other clients, missing exclusions, fee arithmetic and GST treatment, then send the draft to the partner to edit and approve.
  • Send the approved version for e-signature, file the signed copy against the client record and notify the onboarding workflow.

Human checkpoint

The engagement partner edits the draft, sets the final scope and fee, and approves it. Nothing reaches a client without that approval, and AI-drafted text stays highlighted until a person has reviewed it.

Systems it connects

  • Rate card and fee policy
  • E-signature provider
  • Matter or engagement register

Data & consent

Drafting uses the firm's approved library and the current client's scoping notes only; other clients' matter files are excluded from retrieval. Model access runs under business terms that exclude training on firm data. Drafts and signed letters are kept with the client record under the firm's retention policy.

What we deliver

  • Tagged proposal and clause library with owners
  • Template-driven drafting workflow with AI text marked
  • Pre-send checks for names, fees and GST
  • Signed-document filing and onboarding handoff

How we measure it

  • Working days from scoping call to proposal or letter sent
  • Proposal win rate by service line
  • Engagements with signed written terms
  • Partner editing time per draft

Dates, status and client updatesStarter2–4 weeks

Hearing diary, next-date updates and client reminders

After every hearing, the next date is recorded once and drives reminders for the advocate, the clerk and the brief preparation team, plus a short date-only update for clients who have opted in.

Law firms & legal practices

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Next dates are written in a diary or a clerk's register, shared on personal phones and re-typed into several places. Juniors miss preparation windows, clients call the office to ask what happened, and a missed date is discovered only when the matter is called.

Trigger

The clerk or associate records the outcome and next date of a hearing against the matter, or enters the firm's matters from a newly published cause list.

How it runs

  • Capture outcome, next date, purpose and court number in a short form linked to the matter, including the CNR where the court provides one.
  • Create preparation tasks for the matter team, such as brief, compilation and written submissions, with dates working back from the hearing.
  • Send the advocate and clerk reminders before the hearing and a morning list of the day's matters grouped by court.
  • Send clients who opted in at engagement an approved WhatsApp template or email with only the date, court and a matter reference.
  • Flag matters with no next date recorded within a set period after a listed hearing, for the associate to check the official case status.

Human checkpoint

The associate or clerk confirms each next date against the court's cause list or eCourts case status before saving it. Limitation and filing deadlines are calculated and entered by a lawyer, never by the system.

Tools

AAirtablenn8nWBWhatsApp Business PlatformRResendSSlack

Systems it connects

  • Matter management system or matter register
  • eCourts Services case status and cause lists
  • High Court and tribunal cause lists
  • Firm calendar

Data & consent

Client messages contain no strategy or privileged content. Clients opt in to WhatsApp updates in the engagement letter and can opt out at any time. The diary records who entered and who confirmed each date, and access follows matter staffing.

What we deliver

  • Hearing outcome form linked to matters
  • Daily court-wise matter list
  • Advocate, clerk and client reminder templates
  • Missing next-date exception report

How we measure it

  • Hearings with preparation tasks completed on time
  • Next dates confirmed within one working day of hearing
  • Client calls asking for next dates
  • Missed or late appearances

Doing the workStandard4–6 weeks

Legal document assembly from the firm's templates

Legal notices, agreements, affidavits and routine applications are generated from approved templates and clause options using matter data, with every deviation highlighted for the drafting lawyer.

Law firms & legal practices

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Juniors draft routine documents by editing the last similar file, which risks carrying another client's names, facts or terms. Partners then spend review time on formatting and inconsistencies instead of substance, and the firm's preferred clauses drift.

Trigger

A lawyer selects a document type for a matter, such as a legal notice, NDA, leave and license agreement, affidavit or a routine application.

How it runs

  • Pull parties, addresses, dates, amounts and court or forum details from the matter record into a short questionnaire the lawyer completes.
  • Assemble the document from the approved template and the clause options the questionnaire selects, including stamp duty and execution notes maintained by the knowledge team.
  • Highlight every missing field, every optional clause chosen and any wording edited away from the approved version.
  • Optionally have an LLM draft a plain-language cover email to the client, marked as a draft for the lawyer.
  • Save the draft in the document management system against the matter with version control, and route it to the reviewing lawyer.

Human checkpoint

The drafting lawyer reviews and edits every document, and a senior lawyer approves anything that leaves the firm. Lawyers decide clause choices and legal positions; the system only fills approved text.

Tools

PPythonSSupabaseRRetoolACAnthropic Claudenn8n

Systems it connects

  • Document management system such as iManage, NetDocuments or SharePoint
  • Matter management system
  • Approved template and clause library

Data & consent

Only the current matter's data is used. Templates are owned and versioned by a named knowledge lawyer. Generated drafts inherit the matter's access permissions, and client data is never used to train models.

What we deliver

  • Digitized templates and clause library with owners
  • Questionnaire-driven assembly tool
  • Deviation and missing-field report
  • Document management filing with versioning

How we measure it

  • Drafting time for routine documents
  • Review comments per draft
  • Documents built on the current template version
  • Errors found after issue

Doing the workAdvanced6–10 weeks

Knowledge assistant grounded in the firm's own work

Lawyers, CAs and consultants ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn only from the firm's approved precedents, opinions and past deliverables, with citations and matter-level access controls.

Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Years of opinions, pleadings, tax positions and deliverables sit in folders that only their authors can find. Public AI tools cannot be given client documents, and answers without sources are of no use to a professional who must sign the advice.

Trigger

A professional asks a question in the assistant inside the firm's workspace, such as Slack, Microsoft Teams or an internal web app.

How it runs

  • Inventory approved sources with the knowledge owner: precedents, opinions, research memos, past deliverables and checklists, excluding drafts and restricted matters.
  • Index documents with metadata for client, matter, practice area, date and access group, mirroring permissions and information barriers from the document system.
  • Retrieve only passages the user may see, and have the model answer strictly from them with citations to document and paragraph.
  • Decline and say so when sources are missing or conflicting, rather than answering from general knowledge.
  • Log questions, sources used and user feedback, and review a sample each month with the knowledge owner.

Human checkpoint

The professional reads the cited sources before relying on anything and remains responsible for the advice. A named knowledge owner approves what is indexed and reviews flagged answers. The assistant never advises clients directly.

Tools

ACAnthropic ClaudeOOpenAILLlamaIndexQQdrantOOllamaSSlackRRetool

Systems it connects

  • Document management system
  • Practice management system for access groups
  • Licensed research databases, linked rather than copied

Data & consent

Client documents stay in the environment the firm chooses: a cloud model under terms that exclude training on inputs, or a self-hosted model through Ollama for the most sensitive matters. Access mirrors the document system, and logs are kept for quality review and security. Client information is used only for the purposes the client engaged the firm for.

What we deliver

  • Knowledge inventory with owners and exclusions
  • Permission-aware retrieval index
  • Assistant interface with citations
  • Evaluation set and monthly quality review

How we measure it

  • Answers with valid citations in monthly review
  • Questions declined for lack of sources
  • Time to find a relevant precedent
  • Access-control test results

Billing, collections and reviewStandard3–5 weeks

Time capture, billing and fee reminders

Daily nudges keep timesheets current, unbilled work is visible every week, invoices are drafted with GST details for partner approval, and courteous reminders follow overdue fees.

Marketing & creative agencies · Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Time is reconstructed at month end, so hours are lost or vague. Unbilled work sits for weeks because nobody owns the follow-up, invoices are typed by hand, and partners put off awkward fee calls until the amount is large.

Trigger

The end of each working day for timesheets, a weekly schedule for unbilled work, a billing milestone in the engagement terms, or an invoice passing its due date.

How it runs

  • Send each professional a Slack or email nudge listing missing days, with a draft built from calendar events and task activity that they confirm or edit.
  • Produce a weekly unbilled-work report by client, matter or project against the agreed fee, retainer or appearance basis.
  • Draft invoices from approved time or milestones through the Zoho Books API or an import file for Tally Prime, with GSTIN, place of supply and GST, or the reverse-charge note for legal services to business entities.
  • After approval, send the invoice with a payment link from the firm's gateway and log it against the client.
  • Send courteous reminders for overdue invoices by email or an approved WhatsApp utility template on an agreed schedule, pausing automatically for disputed or partner-flagged clients.

Human checkpoint

The engagement partner approves every invoice, write-down and write-off. The partner handles disputed fees and sensitive clients personally, and reminders stop as soon as an account is flagged.

Tools

SSlacknn8nRResendWBWhatsApp Business PlatformMPMicrosoft Power BI

Systems it connects

  • Zoho Books or Tally Prime
  • Time tracking or practice management tool
  • Payment gateway such as Razorpay
  • Calendar

Data & consent

Timesheet drafts use calendar titles and task activity, shown only to the professional before submission. Invoices hold the client's billing and GST details. Reminders carry only the invoice number and amount, sent to the client's billing contact who agreed to receive them.

What we deliver

  • Timesheet nudge and draft workflow
  • Weekly unbilled-work report
  • Invoice drafting with GST fields
  • Overdue reminder sequence with pause rules

How we measure it

  • Timesheets submitted on time
  • Days from work done to invoice
  • Overdue receivables by age
  • Write-offs as a share of billed value
